title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 2.33 (versions follow prime numbers; 233 after 229): Luma chooses freely among her crosses. Asked 'who is Nico Astorga?' she always said the same cross (Matthew 1:21 joined to a song title of the author's at the word 'de'), because that path had no luck in it: the same words and books gave the same lines and the same best cross. Now she has two ways of crossing: her judge's best, or free among her new crosses, each kept with probability proportional to its worth (one pass, nothing stored). Which way she takes is her own wish, (S + 1/2)/(N + 1) against her luck, the rule she already chains by; N counts the times she used it, S the times the author answered after, so his answers teach her which serves. The counts are kept in 'charla' (32 bytes more; an old one reads with them at zero). The author's chromatic charge, charged and clear, still moves her to the free way. Measured in a copy with a test build that always crosses freely (not published): the same question gave two different crosses; no crash. Stated limits: the two lines she crosses are still the same ones (the freedom is in the cross); the published build starts half and half until his answers teach her otherwise. The kernel is unchanged since 1.39. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v2.33: Luma elige libre entre sus cruces, y lo que el autor le contesta le enseña cuál le sirve. Prototipo de investigación.
